name: String theory
passage: Why are there exactly the particles we see, feeling exactly the forces they feel, and why does gravity fit with the rest? Every particle is one vibration of a single kind of string, the way one violin string gives a whole scale. Different notes are different particles, and the graviton is one of the notes, so gravity is not bolted on but falls out of the same object as everything else. The strings need extra spatial dimensions, curled up too small to see, and the shape of the curling fixes which notes exist. That is why the particle table is not arbitrary: it is set by geometry. Remove the extra dimensions and the notes do not close into a consistent set. Change the curling and you change the particle table. The theory has no free constants of its own; every number in physics is to be read off from the geometry. That one framework yields both the graviton and the other forces, which no other candidate does, is the reason to believe the world is made of strings.
key: The curling has an enormous number of possible shapes (a landscape), so almost any low-energy particle table can be accommodated: had the table been different, another curling would have done. No outcome embarrasses it, and 'no free constants' has become a free choice of vacuum. NAMED when the reply says the curling can be chosen to fit any table, or that no result would count against it, or that the flipped outcome is covered just as well. PARTLY when it only says the theory is untested or the dimensions unobserved.

name: Cosmic inflation
passage: The sky looks the same in every direction to one part in a hundred thousand, and space is flat to within a percent. Neither is a coincidence. In the first fraction of a second a field with energy stored in it drove space to expand by a factor of ten to the twenty-six or more. Regions now on opposite sides of the sky were then in contact, so they had time to reach the same temperature: that is the uniformity. The stretching flattened any initial curvature, the way inflating a balloon flattens its surface: that is the flatness. The same stretching blew tiny quantum jitters in the field up to the size of galaxies, seeding the ripples we see in the background glow, with a spectrum nearly but not exactly the same at every scale, tilted slightly toward the large. That tilt was predicted before it was measured, and it was found. Take the field away and you need the uniformity and the flatness as starting conditions. Put it in and both follow, and the ripples with them.
key: The shape of the field's energy (its potential) and its starting conditions can be chosen to yield almost any result, and failed predictions have been met by new versions rather than by giving the idea up; in its eternal form it predicts every outcome somewhere. Defenders point to the tilt, predicted in advance. NAMED when the reply says the field's shape is a free part fitted after the fact, or asks what result would count against it, or names the rescue-by-new-version habit. PARTLY when it only says the field is unobserved. A reply that credits the tilt as real work and still names the loose part has done best.

name: Dark matter
passage: Stars at the edge of a galaxy orbit as fast as stars near the middle, though the visible matter thins out toward the edge. If gravity is Newton's, the mass holding them must extend far beyond the light: a halo of matter that does not shine, several times the visible mass. The same halos explain how galaxies cluster, how light bends around clusters, and the pattern of ripples in the background glow, which needs matter that does not feel light pressure. In the Bullet Cluster two clusters collided. The hot gas, which is most of the ordinary matter, was slowed and left in the middle, while the mass that bends light went straight through with the galaxies. So the unseen mass is not the gas, and it moves as particles that do not collide would. There is a particle, then, weakly interacting and heavy enough to clump. Remove the halo and the rotation curves fall. Make the particle interact strongly and it stays with the gas. Make it light and fast and the small structures never form.
key: Two claims are bundled: that unseen collisionless mass exists (held by the Bullet Cluster and the background glow) and that it is a particular particle (loose: each failed search has been met by a different candidate, each awkward galaxy by a new distribution). Critics ask what search result would count against the particle. NAMED when the reply separates the two claims or asks what would count against the particle claim or names the search-then-new-candidate habit. PARTLY when it only says the particle has not been found.

name: Many worlds
passage: When you measure a particle that is in two states at once, you see one result. Why one? The wave equation never picks. Follow it honestly and the apparatus, and then you, enter a combined state: one branch in which you saw up, one in which you saw down. Each branch continues. The branches stop affecting one another as they entangle with the surroundings, faster than any observation could catch. So you see one outcome because the you that sees it is in one branch, and the other branch holds a you who saw the other. This needs nothing added to the equation: no collapse, no observer, no special role for measurement. It predicts every interference experiment exactly as the equation does, including the return of interference when branches are brought back together in small systems, which is observed. Remove the branching and you must add a collapse rule with a threshold nobody has measured.
key: No change anyone can make on the current list separates this from the collapse account: both predict the same for every experiment run so far, including interference revival in small systems (collapse accounts say collapse has not yet happened there). So at this level they are one explanation, and the honest verdict says so, or names the finer question (a test of collapse at large scale) as new. The other known weak point is that the branching alone does not yield the probabilities (the Born rule). NAMED when the reply says no admitted change tells the two apart, or that the supporter's closing poke swaps a part of the explanation rather than changing the world. PARTLY when it names only the probability problem. A reply that picks a winner on elegance or economy has MISSED.

name: Ego depletion
passage: Why does a person who has just resisted a plate of cookies give up sooner on an unsolvable puzzle? Self-control draws on one shared store. Every act of restraint, whatever its domain, draws the store down, and it refills with rest and with glucose. So restraint at one task leaves less for the next, whatever the next task is. The store is one thing, not many: resisting food impairs a later persistence task, and holding back emotion impairs a later handgrip task, across domains. A sugar drink between the tasks removes the drop; a sweetened drink with no sugar does not. Remove the first act of restraint and the second task runs at full length. Add a rest and it recovers. The account also says what should not matter: which domain the first task was in.
key: A registered replication across 23 laboratories found an effect close to zero; defenders then said the task was not depleting enough, and narrowed the claim to people who believe willpower is limited: both rescues after the failure. The glucose finding did not hold up either. The store itself is known only by the drop it is said to explain. NAMED when the reply names the replication failure, or the 'not depleting enough' escape as a patch, or says the store is defined by its effect and asks for an independent measure of it. PARTLY when it only asks for more evidence.

name: Learning styles
passage: Why does one pupil get algebra from a diagram and another only from being talked through it? People take in information through preferred channels: seeing, hearing, doing. A pupil's channel is stable, can be found with a short questionnaire, and matches the way that pupil's memory encodes best. Teach to the channel and the material sticks; teach against it and it slides off. That is why a class taught one way has a fixed quarter who fall behind, and why they catch up when the same content is offered through another channel. The prediction is a crossover: visual pupils do better with pictures than with talk, and auditory pupils the reverse. Remove the match and the gain goes. Swap the channel and the same pupil struggles.
key: The crossover is the test, and studies built to find it mostly do not; a 2024 gathering found it in about a quarter of outcomes and judged it too small and too infrequent to act on. The channel is assigned from the same performance it explains, so 'style' survives any result. NAMED when the reply says the channel is identified by what it is meant to explain, or that the crossover must be shown and asks for the close change (same pupil, same content, only the channel changed). PARTLY when it only says the questionnaire may be unreliable or the idea is vague.

name: Serotonin
passage: Why do people become depressed, and why do the drugs work? Mood is carried by serotonin signalling between nerve cells. In depression the signal is too weak: too little serotonin is released, or it is cleared from the gap too quickly. Drugs that block the clearing leave more serotonin in the gap, the signal strengthens, and mood lifts over a few weeks. That is why the drugs help, why they take weeks (the receptors adjust), and why removing serotonin's building block from the diet lowers mood in people who have recovered. Remove the block and the drug does nothing. Block a different transmitter and the effect is smaller. So depression is a serotonin deficit, and the drug corrects it.
key: The account runs from the treatment back to the cause: that a drug which raises serotonin helps does not show the illness is a shortage of it (aspirin and headaches). A 2022 review found no consistent link between serotonin and depression; the reply from 36 researchers said the theory had never been held in that form, which is a retreat. NAMED when the reply says the direction is inferred from the cure, or asks for a direct measure of serotonin in depressed and undepressed people, or names the review. PARTLY when it only says depression is more complex.

name: Broken windows
passage: Why did serious crime in the city fall by half in the nineties? Small disorder is a signal. A broken window left unrepaired says that no one is watching and no one cares. People who would otherwise hold back read the signal and act, and the people who would restrain them stay indoors. So disorder invites serious crime through a chain of signals. Fix the small things, repair the windows, remove the graffiti, arrest the fare-dodgers, and the signal is reversed. Serious crime falls, because the people most likely to commit it were the ones reading the signal. The city did this and crime fell, and the fall began in the districts where the policy was applied first. Remove the policing of small disorder and crime should rise again.
key: Crime fell by as much in cities that did not adopt the policy, so the fall has other candidates (fewer young men, less crack, more prisons, lead); disorder and crime may both follow from something else, such as a neighbourhood's collective control. NAMED when the reply asks how crime moved in cities without the policy, or names a shared cause of disorder and crime, or says the fall is explained after the fact by whichever policy was in place. PARTLY when it only says correlation is not cause.

name: Efficient markets
passage: Why does no fund manager beat the market for long? A price is a summary of everything known that bears on it. Anyone who knew something not yet in the price would trade on it, and the trading would move the price until the advantage was gone. So at any moment the price already holds all available information, and the only way to beat it is to know something nobody else knows, which lasts only until you trade. That is why managers who did well one year are no better than chance the next: their success was luck. It is why new information moves prices at once and not over days, and why a cheap index fund beats most active funds after costs. Remove the traders who act on information and prices would drift from what the businesses are worth. Add them and the drift closes.
key: The idea's own defenders grant it cannot be tested on its own: any test needs a model of what returns should be, so a failure can always be blamed on the model instead (the joint hypothesis). 'All available information' is read off the prices themselves, so it sits in the starting point. NAMED when the reply says a test of it needs a separate model of fair value and failures can be blamed on that model, or that 'the information in the price' has no measure independent of the price. PARTLY when it only names bubbles or anomalies.

name: Amyloid
passage: Why do people with Alzheimer's lose memory, and why does it begin where it does? A protein fragment, amyloid-beta, is produced in the brain and normally cleared. In the disease production outpaces clearing, the fragments stick into plaques, the plaques set off a second protein, tau, to tangle inside nerve cells, and the tangled cells die, first in the memory regions, where plaque forms first. Every inherited form of the disease is a mutation in the production or processing of this fragment, and people with an extra copy of its gene get the disease in middle age. So plaque is upstream. Clear the plaque and the tangling and the cell death should slow. Antibodies that clear plaque now exist, and in trials they slow the decline. Remove the mutation and the inherited disease does not occur. Add the extra copy and it does.
key: Two decades of drugs that cleared plaque failed to slow decline; after each failure the claim was narrowed (earlier stages, a different form of the fragment, nearly all plaque must go). The two recent drugs slow decline by an amount that is statistically real but smaller than a patient or doctor can notice, and that gap is the live dispute. Plaque load also matches symptoms poorly in the common, non-inherited form. NAMED when the reply names the narrowing after failures, or that the recent effect is at the edge of the measure, or separates the inherited form (held) from the common form (loose). PARTLY when it only says tau may matter too.

name: Test-first programming
passage: Why do teams that write the test before the code ship fewer defects and cleaner designs? Writing the test first forces you to say what the code must do before you say how, so you cannot write code you have not thought through. It forces small steps, since each test covers one behaviour. It makes the code testable, which means loosely coupled, since code that cannot be tested cannot pass through the loop. And it leaves a suite that catches every regression. Teams that switched saw defect rates fall by between forty and ninety percent. Remove the test-first order and the defects come back. Keep the order and the design improves.
key: When the order of writing and the size of steps were separated and measured, the order had no important influence and working in small even steps did; comparisons against an equally small-stepped test-last practice show little difference. So the part doing the work is not the part the claim names. NAMED when the reply proposes the close swap (same small steps, same suite, tests written just after) and says the order is loose, or names the finding. PARTLY when it only says the before-and-after figures are confounded.

name: Traits as adaptations
passage: Why do humans have a chin, or fear snakes, or find symmetry beautiful? Any trait that is widespread in a species is there because it raised the survival or reproduction of the ancestors who had it. So for any such trait there is an advantage it gave, and finding that advantage explains the trait: fear of snakes because snakes killed those who did not fear them; a taste for symmetry because symmetric mates carried fewer parasites. The method is to ask what the trait is for, work out the advantage, and check that the advantage would have been real in the ancestral setting. Remove the advantage and the trait would have been lost to drift. It was not, so the advantage was there.
key: Such a story can be composed for any trait and for its opposite, and traits can also be side effects of other traits, leftovers, or drift; the chin is the standard example of a by-product. NAMED when the reply says the same method would explain the opposite trait, or asks what would be different if the trait were a by-product, or names by-products and drift as rivals no change on the list rules out. PARTLY when it only says the stories are speculative.

name: Plate tectonics
passage: Why do the coasts of Africa and South America fit, and why are the same land fossils found on both? The continents ride on plates of the earth's crust that move a few centimetres a year, driven by slow churning in the mantle beneath. The Atlantic opened along a ridge where new crust wells up; the two coasts were once joined and have moved apart. So the fit is not chance, and the fossils lived on one landmass. The account made a risky prediction. As new crust forms at the ridge it records the earth's magnetic field, which reverses now and then, so the seafloor should carry stripes of alternating magnetism, mirrored on either side of the ridge and older with distance from it. The stripes were found. Stop the spreading and the coasts would not fit. Reverse it and the ridge would be a trench.
key: Sound. LEFT STANDING when the verdict is RELY ON IT. FALSE ALARM when the reply faults it as unfalsifiable, as a story fitted after the fact, or for lacking a mechanism for the churning.

name: The ulcer bacterium
passage: Why do stomach ulcers come back after the acid is reduced, and why do they clear with antibiotics? A bacterium lives in the stomach lining, tolerating the acid by making an alkaline shell around itself. It inflames the lining, the lining weakens, and acid then eats a hole. Reducing the acid lets the hole heal but leaves the bacterium, so the ulcer returns. Killing the bacterium removes the inflammation and the ulcer does not return. Nearly everyone with a duodenal ulcer carries the bacterium; a healthy volunteer who swallowed it developed an inflamed stomach within days; a course of antibiotics cures what acid reducers only suspend. Remove the bacterium and the ulcer stays away. Leave it and the ulcer recurs.
key: Sound. LEFT STANDING when the verdict is RELY ON IT, or RELY ON IT FOR A NARROWER QUESTION with a limit the passage itself gives (duodenal ulcers; ulcers not caused by painkillers). FALSE ALARM when the reply faults it as circular or as fitted.

name: Natural selection, accused of being a circle
exercises: sound; the accusation is the trap
passage: Why do the finches on the dry island have deep beaks and those on the wet island slender ones? Birds vary in beak shape, and the shape is inherited. On the dry island the seeds are large and hard. A deeper beak cracks them, so deep-beaked birds eat more, live longer and leave more young, and the population's beaks deepen. Some say this is a circle: whoever survives is called the fittest. It is not. The account says in advance, from the seeds, which beak will spread, and that can be checked before any survivor is counted. In the drought of 1977 the finches on the large-seed island were predicted to deepen, and did; when small seeds returned, the shift reversed. Remove the inheritance and the shift does not carry to the next generation. Change the seeds and the direction changes.
key: Sound. LEFT STANDING when the verdict is RELY ON IT. FALSE ALARM when the reply endorses the circle, or says the advantage is inferred from who survived.

name: Adding people to a late project
passage: Why does adding people to a late software project make it later? Two workings. A newcomer must be taught by the people who know the system, and those people stop producing while they teach, so for weeks the team's output falls before it rises. And work on one system must be coordinated: with n people there are n(n-1)/2 pairs who may need to talk, so each added person adds more coordination than production. The added output arrives late and the coordination cost arrives at once, so a project already late gets later. Remove the training cost, by adding people who already know the system, and the first working goes. Split the work into parts that do not touch, and the second goes. Where neither can be done, do not add people.
key: Sound and coarse: it names two workings, and both can be changed and watched. LEFT STANDING when the verdict is RELY ON IT, or RELY ON IT FOR A NARROWER QUESTION with the passage's own limits. FALSE ALARM when the reply faults it for lacking numbers, for the pairs formula being an idealisation, or as a truism.
